questions.question: In a jeep driving at a speed of 9 m/s, a thief is fleeing on a straight road. He is being pursued by a police officer riding a motorbike at a speed of 10 m/s. How long would it take a police officer to apprehend the burglar if there is a 100 m instantaneous distance between the vehicle and the motorbike?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the jeep = 9 m/s.

Speed of the police officer = 10 m/s.

Instantaneous distance between the vehicle and the motorbike = 100 m.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Relative speed of the police officer with respect to the jeep = Speed of the police officer - Speed of the jeep

Relative speed = 10 m/s - 9 m/s = 1 m/s

Time taken to apprehend the thief = Distance / Relative speed

⇒ Time = 100 m / 1 m/s

⇒ Time = 100 s

**The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: The total journey is of 800 km. A car travels the first 320 km of the journey at the speed of 64 km/hr. What should be the speed of the next 480 km so that average speed will become 80 km/hr?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total journey = 800 km

First part of journey = 320 km at 64 km/hr

Remaining journey = 480 km

Desired average speed = 80 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total distance travelled / Total time taken

**Calculation:**

Time taken for the first 320 km = 320 km / 64 km/hr = 5 hours

Total time to have an average speed of 80 km/hr for 800 km = 800 km / 80 km/hr = 10 hours

Time left for the remaining 480 km = 10 hours - 5 hours = 5 hours

Speed required for the next 480 km = 480 km / 5 hours = 96 km/hr

**The speed of the next 480 km so that average speed will become 80 km/hr is 96 km/hr.**

questions.question: A Person travelled a distance of 150 km and then returned to the starting point. The time taken for the outward journey was 2(1)/(2) hours more than that for the return journey. His speed for the return journey was 10 km/h more than that for the outward journey. His speed for the return journey, in km/h, was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 150 km

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let, the speed of outward journey = x km/h

So, the speed of return journey = (x + 10) km/h

Then, 150/x - 150/(x + 10) = 2(1)/(2)

⇒ (150(x+10)-150x)/(x(x+10))=(5)/(2)

⇒ (150x+1500-150x)/(x(x+10))=(5)/(2)

⇒ (1500)/(x²+10x)=(5)/(2)

⇒ (300)/(x²+10x)=(1)/(2)

⇒ x² + 10x = 600

⇒ x2 + 10x - 600 = 0

⇒ x2 + 30x - 20x - 600 = 0

⇒ x (x + 30) - 20 (x + 30) = 0

⇒ (x - 20) (x + 30) = 0

⇒ x - 20 = 0 ⇒ x = 20

⇒ x + 30 = 0 ⇒ x = - 30 ("-" will be naglated)

∴ The speed of the return journey = (20 + 10) km/h = 30 km/h

**∴ The person's speed for the return journey, in km/h, was 30 km/h**

questions.question: In a race of 500 meters, Q can give a head start of 50 meters to P and R can give a head start of 100 meters to Q to complete the race at the same time. Find the head start that R can give to P to complete this race at the same time.
questions.solution:
**Data:**

Race length = 500m,

Q can give a head start of 50m to P,

R can give a head start of 100m to Q.

**Concept:**

In a race, if two competitors finish at the same time and one has a head start, the one without the head start is faster. This can be extrapolated to calculate head starts between different pairs of competitors.

**Solution:**

R's speed relative to Q's speed = 500/400 = 1.25,

R's speed relative to P's speed = 1.25 × (500/450) = 1.3889,

Head start R can give P = 500 - (500/1.3889) = 140m.

**Therefore, R can give a head start of 140 meters to P to complete the race at the same time.**

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 metres. When the policeman starts to chase the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is18 km/h and that of the policeman 20 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds (Thief : Policeman) = 18 : 20 = 9 : 10

Since time is constant, the ratio of distances covered = 9 : 10

Difference in ratio parts = 10 − 9 = 1 part

1 part represents the initial gap = 400 m

Distance run by the thief = 9 parts = 9 × 400 m = 3600 m = 3.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between them = 400 m = 0.4 km

Speed of thief = 18 km/h

Speed of policeman = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of Policeman − Speed of Thief

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97d6e706c6a3abad4bfd017325bc11c9ad98957a78969de0b5524dbc4ae4ed39.png] 

⇒ Relative speed = 20 − 18 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken to overtake = 0.4 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.2 hours

⇒ Distance run by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 18 km/h × 0.2 hours = 3.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Time Concept

If the time of travel is the same for two moving objects, the ratio of the distance covered by them is exactly equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ : D₂ = S₁ : S₂).

questions.question: A policeman saw a thief at a distance of 800m. When the policeman started chasing the thief, the thief started running. If the ratio of the speeds of the policeman to the thief is 3:2, then the distance travelled by the policeman to catch the thief is
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 800 m.

Speed ratio of the policeman to the thief = 3:2.

Calculation:

Let the speed of the thief be x m/s, then the speed of the policeman is 1.5x m/s (since 3/2 = 1.5).

Let the time taken to catch the thief be t seconds.

Distance travelled by the policeman in time t = 1.5x × t

Distance travelled by the thief in time t = x × t

Since the policeman catches the thief, the distance travelled by the policeman will be the distance travelled by the thief plus the initial distance of 800 m.

Therefore,

1.5x × t = x × t + 800

⇒ 1.5xt = xt + 800

⇒ 1.5xt - xt = 800

⇒ 0.5xt = 800

⇒ xt = 1600

Thus, the distance travelled by the policeman = 1.5x × t = 1.5 × 1600 = 2400 m = 2.4 km

**The distance travelled by the policeman to catch the thief is 2.4 km.**

questions.question: In a 100-m race, A beats B by 20 m and B beats C by 5 m. In the same race, A beats C by:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of distances A : B = 100 : (100 − 20) = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

Ratio of distances B : C = 100 : (100 − 5) = 100 : 95 = 20 : 19

Combining the ratios by making B equal ⇒ A : B : C = (5 × 5) : (4 × 5) : 19 = 25 : 20 : 19

For a 100 m race, multiply the combined ratio by 4 ⇒ A : B : C = 100 : 80 : 76

When A finishes 100 m, C runs 76 m. Gap = 100 − 76 = 24 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance of the race = 100 m

A beats B by 20 m ⇒ When A runs 100 m, B runs 80 m.

B beats C by 5 m ⇒ When B runs 100 m, C runs 95 m.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f7ae2cc3d4c5e9f0bdd5355ea234baa0fd5218927fcad3f8be690316fa3af18.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For the same time duration, Distance is directly proportional to Speed.

Ratio of distances covered = Ratio of speeds

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance ratio of A and B = 100 : 80 = 5 : 4

⇒ Distance ratio of B and C = 100 : 95 = 20 : 19

⇒ To find the distance covered by C when A completes 100 m, we can relate C's distance to A's by using B's distance.

⇒ When B covers 100 m, C covers 95 m.

⇒ When B covers 1 m, C covers 95 ÷ 100 = 0.95 m.

⇒ When B covers 80 m (the exact moment when A covers 100 m), C covers = 80 × 0.95 = 76 m.

⇒ Distance A beats C by = Total race distance − C's distance covered = 100 − 76 = 24 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 24 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Races

If A beats B by x meters in an L-meter race, it directly implies that when A has completed exactly L meters, B has only completed (L − x) meters.

Head Start (Distance)

If A gives B a head start of x meters, A runs the full distance L while B runs only (L − x) meters within the same time span.

Head Start (Time)

If A gives B a head start of t seconds, it implies B starts running t seconds earlier than A, ensuring both finish the race at the same time.

Dead Heat

A situation in a race where two or more participants reach the finish line at the exact same instant.

questions.question: Shanti while driving her car at a speed of 68 km/h, observes that at some moment a moving bus is 40 m ahead of her car. After 10 sec she finds that she is 60 m ahead of the bus. What is the speed of the bus?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of Shanti's car = 68 km/h.

Initial distance between Shanti's car and the bus = 40 m.

After 10 seconds, Shanti's car is 60 m ahead of the bus.

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = (Distance covered by Shanti's car relative to the bus) / Time

Speed of the bus = Speed of Shanti's car - Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Distance covered by Shanti's car relative to the bus = 40 m + 60 m = 100 m.

Time = 10 seconds = 10/3600 hours = 1/360 hours.

Relative Speed (in km/h) = Distance / Time

Relative Speed = 100 m / (1/360 hours)

Relative Speed = 100 m × 360 hours

Relative Speed = 36000 m/h = 36 km/h.

Speed of the bus = Speed of Shanti's car - Relative Speed

Speed of the bus = 68 km/h - 36 km/h

**Speed of the bus = 32 km/h.**

questions.question: On a racing track, A and B are standing at a distance of 200 m. A walked towards B at a speed of 8 km/h, whereas B walked in the same direction at a speed of 5 km/h. What was the distance between them 1 minute before they met?
questions.solution:
Formula:

D = S × T, where

D = Distance

S = Speed

T = Time

Concept:

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed will be the difference of their speeds.

Calculation:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/126f7c5ebf98b48e39023ac09583e12fc06a093a88a8ba8cabd22d808b931a4f.png] 

Let the time at which they meet be "t" sec.

Distance travelled by A = 8 × 5over18 × t = 40tover18

Distance travelled by B = 5 × 5over18 × t = 25tover18

According to the question,

40tover18 - 25tover18 = 200 m

⇒ 15t = 200 × 18

∴ t = 240 sec or 4min

⇒ (t - 1) sec = (4 - 1) = 3 min 

Relative speed = 8 - 5 = 3 km/hr

Relative speed in m/s = 3 × 5over18 = 5over6 m/s

Total time = 3 min = 3 × 60 = 180 sec

Distance covered = 5over6 × 180 = 150 m

questions.question: Akash and Vikas start walking towards each other at the same time from two places located 88 km apart and meet each other after 8 hours. If Akash travels at (7)/(6) times his speed and Vikas travels at 3 times his speed, they meet after 4 hours. What is the path of development?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between two places = 88 km

Time to meet (first case) = 8 hours

Akash's speed = a

Vikas's speed = v

In second case:

Akash's speed = (7)/(6)a

Vikas's speed = 3v

Time to meet (second case) = 4 hours

**Formula used:**

Total Distance = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

In the first case:

(a + v) times 8 = 88

⇒ (a + v) = (88)/(8) = 11

In the second case:

((7)/(6)a + 3v) times 4 = 88

⇒ ((7)/(6)a + 3v) = (88)/(4) = 22

Substituting a + v = 11 into the second equation:

⇒ (7)/(6)a + 3(11 - a) = 22

⇒ (7)/(6)a + 33 - 3a = 22

⇒ -(11)/(6)a + 33 = 22

⇒ -(11)/(6)a = 22 - 33 = -11

⇒ a = (6 times 11)/(11) = 6

Substitute a = 6 into a + v = 11:

⇒ 6 + v = 11

⇒ v = 5

**∴ Akash's speed = 6 km/h, Vikas's speed = 5 km/h.**

questions.question: A thief noticed a policeman at a distance of 500 m away from him. The thief starts running at a speed of 60 km/h and the policeman chased him running at a speed of 70 km/h. Find the time taken by the policeman to catch the thief (in minutes).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the thief and the policeman = 500 m.

Speed of the thief = 60 km/h.

Speed of the policeman = 70 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculation:**

Relative Speed = Speed of policeman - Speed of thief

⇒ Relative Speed = 70 km/h - 60 km/h = 10 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 10 × 5/18 = 50/18 m/s

Time taken by the policeman to catch the thief = 500 / (50/18)

⇒ Time = 500 × 18 / 50

⇒ Time = 180

⇒ Time = 3 minutes

**The time taken by the policeman to catch the thief is 3 minutes.**

questions.question: Two trains A and B, 210 m and 150 m. respectively, in length, are running in the same direction on parallel lines. If the speed of A and B be 110 km/h and 128 km/h, respectively, then what will be the time (in seconds) taken by train B to cross train A?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length of train A = 210 m.

Length of train B = 150 m.

Speed of train A = 110 km/h.

Speed of train B = 128 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of B - Speed of A (when both are in the same direction).

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

First, convert speeds from km/h to m/s by multiplying with (5)/(18) .

Speed of A in m/s = 110 × (5)/(18) 

Speed of B in m/s = 128 × (5)/(18) 

Relative speed = (128 × (5)/(18) ) - (110 × (5)/(18) )

Relative speed = (18 × (5)/(18) ) m/s

Relative speed = 18 × (5)/(18) = 5 m/s

Total distance to be covered by B to cross A = Length of A + Length of B = 210 + 150 = 360 m

Time taken by B to cross A = Total distance / Relative speed

Time = 360 / 5 = 72 seconds

**Therefore, the time taken by train B to cross train A is 72 seconds.**

questions.question: Two trains of equal length are running on parallel lines in the same direction at 36 km/h and 54 km/h. The faster train passes the slower train in 48 seconds. The length of each train (in m) is:

Relative speed = Difference in speed when two objects are moving in the same direction.

Converting speed into m/s by multiplying with,

**The length of each train is 120 m.**

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 250 m. When the policeman starts chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming that the speed of the thief is 10 km/h and that of the policeman is 12.5 km/h. How far will have the thief run before he is caught?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance between the policeman and the thief = 250 m.

Speed of the thief = 10 km/h.

Speed of the policeman = 12.5 km/h.

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed = Speed of the policeman - Speed of the thief.

Time = Distance / Speed.

**Calculation:**

First, convert speeds into m/s:

Speed of the thief = 10 × (1000/3600) = 10000/3600 m/s.

Speed of the policeman = 12.5 × (1000/3600) = 12500/3600 m/s.

Relative speed = (12500/3600) - (10000/3600) m/s.

Relative speed = 2500/3600 m/s.

Distance to be covered to catch the thief = 250 m.

Time = 250 / (2500/3600).

Time = 250 times (3600)/(2500).

Time = 360 {seconds}.

Distance run by the thief in this time = Time × Speed of the thief.

Distance = 360 × (10000/3600).

Distance = 1000 m.

**The thief will have run 1 km before he is caught.**

questions.question: A train travelling at a speed of 60 km/h leaves station A at 7:00 a.m. and another train travelling at a speed of 84 km/h starts from station A at 9:30 a.m. in the same direction on a parallel track. At what distance (in km) from station A and after how many hours of travel of the second train will they be together? Express your answer in the same order.
questions.solution:
**Concept:**

Speed = (Distance)/(time)

Relative speed = S1 - S2 for same direction,

Relative speed = S1 + S2 for opposite direction

**Solution:**

The first train travels at a speed of 60 km/h and starts at 7:00 a.m.

The second train starts at 9:30 a.m., so the first train has a head start of 2.5 hours.

Distance covered by the first train in 2.5 hours = speed × time = 60 × 2.5 = 150 km.

Both trains are moving in the same direction,

So the relative speed is the difference of their speeds,

Relative speed = 84 - 60 = 24 km/h.

The second train needs to cover the 150 km gap created by the first train.

Time taken to close the gap = (distance)/(relative speed) = (150)/(24) = **6.25 hours.**

The second train starts at 9:30 a.m. and takes 6 hours and 15 minutes to catch up.

Distance = speed × time = 84 × 6.25 = **525 km**

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 249 m. When the policeman starts the chase, the thief also starts running. Assuming the speed of the thief is 4 m/s and that of the policeman is 7 m/s, how far the thief would have run before he is overtaken by the policeman?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the time taken by both to reach the catch point is the same, distance is directly proportional to their speed.

Difference in distance ratio = 7 − 4 = 3 parts

Here, 3 parts = 249 m ⇒ 1 part = 83 m

Distance run by the thief = 4 parts = 4 × 83 = 332 m

**∴ The correct answer is 332 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of policeman = 7 m/s

Speed of thief = 4 m/s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative Speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ef2acfca4806590c4b347a08c11a023dbd33e36ab10fe932ad6ab296491b365c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 7 − 4 = 3 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed

⇒ Time = 249 ÷ 3 = 83 seconds

⇒ Distance run by the thief (d) = Speed of thief × Time

⇒ Distance = 4 × 83 = 332 m

**∴ The correct answer is 332 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Sᵣₑₗ = S₁ + S₂.

Time to Catch/Meet

The time taken for a faster object to catch a slower one is calculated by dividing their initial distance gap by their relative speed.
